content:
Vice President JD Vance made a slip of the tongue about his political opponents on Monday, insisting it was an accident — but he couldn't help but keep laughing.

Speaking at a rally in Greensboro, North Carolina, the vice president said voters should support Republican Senate candidate Michael Whatley because "we need someone who can fight back against the fart-wing left."

Yes, you can re-read those last two words. We'll wait.

While rally attendees dutifully clapped along, Vance felt the need to explain his "fart" pun.

"You may not have noticed this, but I — I typically don't slip up, but I called them the 'fart-wing left' instead of the 'far left,'" Vance explained. "I promise it was an accident," he said.

He then loudly speculated how the "fake news" would react, though he himself seemed more delighted to repeat the phrase.

"So fake news will accuse me of using the wrong word," Vance said. He added: "I promise I didn't mean to call them the 'fart-wing left'; I meant to call them the 'far left.'"

As you can see in the clip below, Vance was laughing like a kid who got away with sneaking a cookie.

Social media confirmed the childishness of Vance's so-called insult.

Vance's "fart-wing left" insult comes just months after President Donald Trump bragged about coining the term "Dumocrats" — meaning stupid Democrats — for the Democratic Party.

The president explained: "I took out the letter 'b' because most people didn't know 'dumb' ended with a 'b.'"
